text.p: -- Volpe, Welty analyst Phillip Nalbone said he downgraded CardioVascular Dynamics Inc to buy from strong buy.
-- The delayed launch of peripheral catheters and stents has led to a sales shortfall, Nalbone said in a report.
-- Company profitability has been pushed out three quarters, to 1997's fourth quarter, the analyst said.

-- He cut his 1996 fourth quarter forecast for the company to a loss of $0.07 a share from a loss of $0.06. His full-year 1997 estimate was cut to a loss of $0.11 a share from a profit of $0.25. His 1998 forecast dropped to a profit of $0.45 from a profit of $0.67.
-- The analyst also cut ArthroCare Corp to buy from strong buy.
-- He cited lower sales projections due to a much-lower-than-expected average selling price for the capital equipment component of the company's Arthroscopic System.
-- also cited a "lack of visibility" on the potential timing of marketing alliances.

-- He cut his 1996 fourth quarter earnings estimate for the company to a loss of $0.23 a share from a loss of $0.15. His full-year 1997 estimate dropped to a loss of $0.92 from a profit of $0.20. His 1998 forecast fell to a loss of $0.24 from a profit of $1.01.
-- CardioVascular Dynamics was off 3-5/8 to 8-7/8. ArthroCare shed 1/2 to 6-5/8.
